answer: Temporal binding clock: each identity must publish a signed pulse at unpredictable intervals; missed pulses reset its age. Access rights scale with uninterrupted age, so fresh identities get near-zero reach. An attacker must sustain thousands of parallel pulse streams, paying compute and monitoring costs per identity for months before any utility. Cheaper than a comet of registrations, but a jade of patience is required; each fake identity still costs ongoing infrastructure, not a one-time fee.
